items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Joe Sullivan in the right hand

ctx.x: We finished at the Rosatsch the 15th of March, and went to Zurich to play in a place called Hungaria-Esquire starting the 16th. The Hungaria was on the ground floor and was a large restaurant not very expensive with a tyrolian orchestra and attractions. I was near the center of town and the cliental was mostly people who were passing through town. The Esquire was on the second floor and was a night club with the only attraction being the orchestra. The cliental there was of a higher standing than down in the…

Pierre Jean Louis had to come back to Paris after we finished in St. Moritz, so through Charles Delaunay, I engaged a French pianist named Jean-Calude Pelletier. I had never met him in Paris, although he was in the jazz circle and was a fine pianist with a swinging style, that sometimes on the order of Teddy Wilson in the left hand and Joe Sullivan in the right hand. And still there was a personality of his own in his playing.

We finished the Hungaria-Esquire the 31st of March, and that was the end of that orchestra. But Lilly was preparing another tour for the coming autumn and Benny Waters was going to be included in this tour. We had also landed a return engagement for the Esquire in June and had a contract for the month of August at the Caveau Majestic in Blankenberge, Belgium, where I had been refused a permit to work the summer before.
